assessment: The observations support investigating allocation and change coordination, but do not establish that sufficient compatible capacity exists. Aggregate vacancy cannot demonstrate satisfaction of equipment-specific or evening demand. Both proposed interaction benefits are hypotheses.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross elicited acceptable windows, equipment and required rehearsal duration with protected 60-minute cores plus requested extensions at the request-to-room allocation interface. Flexibility information could make shorter cores useful without converting longer rehearsal needs into apparent successes.
openings.delta: Recording preferences alone leaves inherited 90-minute boundaries; shortening bookings alone may expose time nobody can use. Joint allocation could pack compatible requests into gaps and reserve piano capacity for verified needs.
openings.prediction: Against both single-mechanism schedules, the combined schedule meets more complete stated needs within acceptable windows, while retaining every requested weekly minimum and both performances.
openings.probe: Use short telephone or in-person conversations to collect actual needs. On the same eight-week demand, compare inherited allocation, preference-aware 90-minute allocation, flexible-duration allocation retaining inherited starts, and the combination. Count fully met needs, guaranteed minima, equipment mismatches and preparation minutes; reject schedules violating constraints.
assumptions: Some groups can use different starts or durations; this is unmeasured.
Jointly feasible minimum slots exist within the two rooms and staffed hours.
A 60-minute guarantee is not automatically a fully met rehearsal need.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross a queue of preauthorized acceptable replacement slots with one authoritative desk ledger at the change-commit interface. A released slot can trigger one confirmed reassignment before synchronized calendar copies are issued.
openings.delta: A queue alone can propagate stale availability; a ledger alone does not identify who can use a release. Their interaction could convert changes into usable rehearsals with fewer repeated negotiations and conflicting expectations.
openings.prediction: The combination produces more accepted reassignments than the ledger alone and fewer conflicting confirmations than the queue alone, without increasing administrative minutes per change.
openings.probe: Replay documented changes with contacts' stated permissions under queue-only, ledger-only and combined rules; measure accepted placements, conflicting confirmations and handling time. Confirm real changes by phone or in person. Never release a weekly minimum without a confirmed replacement; lock performances and existing opening hours.
assumptions: Contacts can preauthorize alternatives without repeated negotiation.
The desk can maintain the authoritative ledger and refresh copies within the two-hour weekly administration ceiling.
